description: Browser-native personal AI assistant. Zero infrastructure, the browser is the server.

summary.one_liner: A browser-only personal AI assistant that runs entirely in a browser tab as a PWA, using the Anthropic API with no backend server.
summary.what_it_does: OpenBrowserClaw is a personal AI chat assistant built as a static web app (PWA) written in TypeScript. The orchestrator runs on the main thread, routing messages and handling a state machine and cron-based task scheduling, while a Web Worker runs the Claude tool-use loop against the raw Anthropic API. Claude can call tools including bash (in an optional WebVM Alpine Linux emulator), a JavaScript eval tool, file read/write/list tools over a per-group OPFS workspace, a fetch_url tool, an update_memory tool that persists to CLAUDE.md, and a create_task tool for recurring cron jobs. Data is stored in IndexedDB and OPFS, and API keys are encrypted with AES-256-GCM using a non-extractable CryptoKey. Channels are the built-in browser chat and an optional Telegram bot that uses only HTTPS. The project describes itself as a browser-only reimplementation of NanoClaw.
use_cases: personal AI chat assistant in the browser
run Claude with tool use without a server
self-hosted-free AI assistant as a static site
chat with an AI assistant through a Telegram bot
scheduled recurring AI tasks in the browser
browser-based sandboxed shell and JavaScript execution
how_to_run: Open the local URL in a browser, paste your Anthropic API key, and start chatting.
npm run build (produces static files in dist/ for any static host)
notable: Zero infrastructure: deploys as plain HTML, CSS, and JS to any static host with no server
Zero runtime npm dependencies, per the README comparison table
Agent runs in a Web Worker separate from the UI thread
Bash tool runs in an in-browser Alpine Linux VM via v86/WASM (optional)
Explicit security section listing known gaps such as eval-based JS tool and plaintext Telegram token
caveats: Background tasks use setInterval, so the browser tab must stay open for scheduled tasks and Telegram replies
The bash tool needs manually downloaded v86 and Alpine rootfs files; without them only the error-returning fallback works
Described as a proof of concept; the Telegram bot token is stored in plaintext and outgoing HTTP has no confirmation step
